correctness.rationale: All objects, the four Seidel-switch inputs and both neighborhood conventions are explicitly defined. For each k<=4 and each graph/convention, both standalone programs enumerate every one of binomial(28,k) supports, every possible center, and all requested Boolean traces; both agree on all 193264 support/family outcomes, the eight five-entry polynomial vectors, and four open maximal-triple counts. Degree and common-neighbor identities are checked for all vertices and pairs. Because there are only 28 concepts, no 5-query support can realize 32 traces, so the enumerated coefficients are complete in all degrees. For every shattered triple the scripts test whether it is contained in a shattered quadruple; all shattered pairs extend. The monograph independently supplies the classification of precisely four graph classes. There are no extrapolations, unproved infinite extensions, or numerical approximations.

originality.rationale: The three Chang open- and closed-neighborhood coefficient vectors and their maximal-triple/purity classification are absent from the inspected exact-source and nearest published work. The previously determined triangular T8 rows are explicitly prior, as are the four-class Chang graph classification, four-round logical separations, and neighborhood-complex homology. This is evidence-limited originality, not an assertion of globally proved priority.

value.rationale: Neighborhood shattering is a natural set-system invariant that extracts all-labeling expressivity from graph adjacency. The three Chang graphs are the canonical counterexamples to uniqueness of the triangular strongly regular parameters, and complete exact profiles make a motivated comparison at fixed order 28, not an arbitrary finite graph slice. Despite identical parameters and identical scalar VC=4, the four graphs have pairwise distinct open and closed shattering polynomials, while the triangular case is pure and the three Chang cases have maximal triples and quadruples. The exact maximal-triple census is a coherent structural classification complementing prior homology and logical distinctions. No unsupported broad theorem is inferred.
